source.title: LTP at Hilar Mossy Cell-Dentate Granule Cell Synapses Modulates Dentate Gyrus Output by Increasing Excitation/Inhibition Balance.

confidence_rationale: Grounds the completion-set partner HPL-9 named for MECH-147: hilar mossy cells set the dentate excitation/inhibition balance (both an associative GC feedback loop AND feed-forward GABAergic inhibition onto GCs) that governs DG output sparsity. Confidence moderate because the paper measures synaptic plasticity / E-I balance, not pattern separation directly -- it establishes the partner circuit, not the separation consequence.
failure_signatures: The study measures MC-GC synaptic plasticity and its effect on E/I balance and GC output; it does NOT directly test that mossy-cell-mediated inhibition improves pattern separation. The link from E/I-balance control to separation is inferred (the authors note possible relevance to pattern separation and epilepsy).

mapping.source_claim_statement: Hilar mossy cells form an associative positive-feedback loop with dentate granule cells AND synapse onto GABAergic interneurons that mediate feed-forward inhibition onto granule cells; LTP at mossy-cell->granule-cell synapses increases the excitation/inhibition balance and enhances granule-cell output.
mapping.ree_translation: Grounds the co-constitutive INHIBITORY partner MECH-147 presupposes. The HPL-9 node flagged that a DG-style separation layer is not self-sufficient: the hilar mossy-cell circuit (excitatory feedback + recruited feed-forward inhibition) sets the E/I balance that controls how sparse, and therefore how decorrelated, granule-cell output is. A REE separation layer built as bare sparse expansion, without an analog of this E/I-balance control, omits the mechanism that actually tunes sparsity.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper establishes the partner circuit and its control over DG output sparsity via E/I balance; it does not demonstrate the downstream separation benefit. The separation consequence is the inference, and the regulation is shown via synaptic plasticity (LTP) rather than as a static architectural requirement.
mapping.source_context: Rodent (mouse/rat) hippocampal slice electrophysiology; optogenetic and pharmacological dissection of mossy-cell -> granule-cell and disynaptic inhibitory pathways.

confidence_components.notes: High-quality primary Neuron ephys. Mapping fidelity moderate: grounds the EXISTENCE and output-control role of the mossy-cell/feed-forward-inhibition partner, not the separation consequence per se. Pairs with Leutgeb 2007 (separation result) to complete the DG circuit picture.
